Resume data aggregation

resume_cycle_aggregation.Rd

If aggregation for a particular cycle has been started but not completed, this function can be used to easily resume aggregation from where it was stopped.

Usage

resume_cycle_aggregation(
  folder_name,
  working_directory = getwd(),
  stop_after_n_splits = NULL,
  input_data_in_chunks = FALSE,
  final_chunk = FALSE
)

Arguments

folder_name

Name of main results folder for this cycle (not including path)

working_directory

Location of the main results folder for this cycle (path only), defaults to getwd().

stop_after_n_splits

Use this to stop aggregation after a given number of splits. Aggregation can then be resumed at a later date (again).

input_data_in_chunks

Option to pre-split input data. Only use this if your data is too large to load into R in one go (otherwise just use split_size). This should match what was used for the initial call of aggregate_data().

final_chunk

If you have pre-split your input data, use this to indicate when you are running the last chunk of your input data. This will trigger the function to combine all the temporary results at the end. This should match what was used for the initial call of aggregate_data().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Resume a previously interrupted aggregation
resume_cycle_aggregation(
  folder_name = "RCA_COVID_TEST_SITE_20220101-20220131",
  working_directory = "~/Documents/RCA_COVID/"
)
} # }
